To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

asthma control status was longitudinally associated with asthma-specific quality of life through nighttime sleep quality (difficulty falling asleep and getting back to sleep) and daytime sleepiness among children with asthma.
asthma control status is associated directly and indirectly with asthma-specific HROL.
asthma control status is directly and indirectly (through nighttime sleep quality and sleepiness) associated with asthma-specific health-related quality of Life in children with asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship among asthma control status, nighttime sleep quality, daytime sleepiness and HRQOL in children with asthma.
the relationship between asthma control and sleep problems in children with asthma, and the impact of sleep problems on asthma-related HRQOL.
the longitudinal associations among asthma control status, sleep problems, daytime sleepiness, and health-related QoL in children with asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
poor control of asthma is associated with poor HRQOL, which is mediated by sleep problems.

asthma control status has a direct effect on asthma-specific HRqOL at both within and between subject levels, and this effect is mediated by daytime sleepiness and nighttime sleep quality at within and between subject level, respectively.
asthma control status is associated to HRQOL in asthmatic children through the mediation of nighttime sleep quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

asthma control status is associated directly with asthma-specific HRQL and this association is influenced indirectly by nighttime sleep quality at within-subject, and by daytime sleepiness and nighttime sleep quality at between-subject levels.
asthma control is directly associated with HRQOL in children with asthma, and this association may be mediated by nighttime sleep problems.
asthma control status is associated asthma-specific HRQoL through the mechanism of sleep problems in asthmatic children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
asthma control, sleep quality, and daytime sleepiness are all important to consider when assessing the quality of life in patients with asthma.
sleep problems are an important mediator of the relationship between asthma control status and asthma-specific HRqOL.
sleep problems are a critical component of asthma control, and that addressing them can improve asthma-specific quality of life for children with asthma.
